react_result.final_narrative_text: The differential metabolite set is dominated by oxidized lipid mediators and methyl-group donors, defining two intersecting biological axes. The primary signal is arachidonic acid metabolism (KEGG:hsa00590), which achieves rank 1 in the Mummichog m/z-direct analysis (p=0.0053) with complete pathway overlap — all five input eicosanoids (8(S)-HPETE, 16(R)-HETE, 19(S)-HETE, 11,12,15-THETA, and thromboxane) map directly to this pathway. The same pathway surfaces in MetaboAnalystR KEGG PSEA at rank 5 (p=0.106) via the 11,12,15-THETA hit. The secondary axis involves retinoid signalling and methyltransferase biology: RaMP ORA identifies Signaling by Nuclear Receptors (REACT:R-HSA-9006931, FDR=0.00145) driven by 4-hydroxyretinoic acid and S-adenosylmethionine, and MetaboAnalystR independently hits Retinol metabolism (KEGG:hsa00830, p=0.042) through the same 4-hydroxyretinoic acid. Theophylline (KEGG:C07130) appears in Mummichog as an adenosine-receptor antagonist consistent with inflammatory signalling crosstalk. The convergence of an eicosanoid storm (five HETEs/HPETE/THETA/thromboxane) with a retinoid-methylation signal points to a treatment effect that simultaneously activates the COX/LOX axis and perturbs nuclear-receptor transcriptional regulation via SAM-dependent methylation. Uridine 5'-diphosphate (KEGG:C00015) participates in glycosylation and nucleotide-sugar metabolism, consistent with downstream remodeling of cell-surface glycosphingolipids.
